title: Espresso shift GPU checklist
content:
ESPRESSO SHIFT — quick run (25–40m)

Context: short solo shift between meetings. Focus = keep serving pools healthy, triage any immediate regressions, and leave readable handoff if something is open.

1) 5m startup checks (high priority)
- slack: #gpu-ops and #platform-alerts — scan for any active incident threads (search "P0" or "OOM").
- grafana: open cluster-overview (region-west, -east) — check GPU-utilation, queue-burn, and preemptible eviction spikes.
- nvidia checks: run `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,memory.used,memory.total,utilization.gpu --format=csv` on the three hottest nodes; capture output to note.
- spotty-node quick query: `kubectl get nodes -l preemptible=true -o wide` — if >30% NotReady, ping SRE on-call.

2) 10m triage (if anomaly found)
- if a node shows 90% mem and not high GPU util, suspect leaked KV cache; run `ps aux | grep python` and check long-running pods on that node.
- drain pattern (temporary): `kubectl cordon <node>` then `kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --pod-selector='app!=infra-sidecar'` — note: only for nodes with CLEAR evidence.
- for recurrent cache leaks: create ticket & add to backlog: JIRA-OPS-4123 (linked).

3) 10–20m operational housekeeping
- Log rotate: confirm last rotation for inference logs (s3 path /prod/inference/logs/) — if >7d, run retention job or open tiny PR.
- Cache hit check: run small query against redis prefix-cache stats: `redis-cli -h cache-host INFO keyspace` and check prefix hit ratio (quick heuristic: look at key lookups vs hits).
- Autoscaler health: snapshot current desired/actual for gpu-pool-autoscale (copy values into this doc). If desired >> actual and pending pods exist, escalate to infra-auto-scaling-sre.

4) Quick mitigations (if latency spike)
- fallback route: switch route to a smaller context model variant (hosted routing) via quick rollback command in console (console -> routes -> choose fallback -> enable). Note down route id and reason.
- temporary quantized flavor: trigger canary on dedicated pool (if available) and keep 10% traffic.

5) Notes-to-self & debugging snippets
- frequently-used commands:
  - `kubectl top pods -n inference | sort -k3 -nr | head`
  - `ssh gpu-node-XX sudo journalctl -u orchestration --since "1h" --no-pager | tail -n 200`
  - `python /usr/local/bin/kv-cache-check.py --threshold=80` (local script)
- when I see repeated kernel OOMs, check dmesg for "Out of memory" and grep for container id mapping.

6) Hand-off checklist if I leave an open item
- write short summary in incident-triage thread with: what I saw, node IDs, commands run, and why I drained (if I did).
- add next steps + owner: e.g., "Follow-up: add eviction metric alert (owner: Mateo)".
- attach snippets (nvidia-smi output, kubectl drain logs) to the Jira ticket.

7) Quick todo (for the rest of the day)
- add a small health alert for prefix-cache-hit < 0.6 (low effort) — followup PR to infra-alerts repo.
- investigate recurring pod X restart pattern (candidate: env var mismatch after deploy), link to PR 987.
- clean up old node provisioning templates in zone-us-west-2 (deprovisioning stalled templates cause drift).

Open questions / scribbles
- Could we expose GPU mem fragmentation metric? (ask research infra team)
- Is there a cheap way to simulate KV cache pressure in staging without burning prod tokens? (experiment idea: small-scale synthetic workload)

End-of-shift quick note: leave this file with timestamp and any clippings I pasted from terminal. If nothing unresolved — mark status = final and add short note in #gpu-ops.
